# UI Requirements

What the owner needs from the interface. The UI reviewer reads this file at the start of every turn and reviews against it. The coding agent reads it too.

**Owned by the owner.** Agents do not edit this file. The UI reviewer proposes changes in its review; the owner decides and edits here. Requirement ids are permanent: change the text of a requirement, or mark it `Retired`, but do not reuse an id.

## Who the user is

One adult beginner who cannot yet sing in tune and does not read music. Practises alone with headphones, on a laptop at a desk and on an iPhone in portrait, often propped up at arm's length. Looks at the screen while singing, so the important information must be readable at a glance.

## Requirements

### The piano and live feedback

| Id | Requirement |
|----|-------------|
| UR-01 | The piano keyboard is the main visualization on every training screen. There is no scrolling piano roll. |
| UR-02 | The note to sing and the note being sung are shown on the piano at the same time, in real time, and are clearly different from each other. |
| UR-03 | It is obvious at a glance whether the sung note matches the target (one colour for a match, another for off-target), and how far flat or sharp it is. |
| UR-04 | Singing in the wrong octave is visibly wrong on the piano: the sung key is shown an octave from the target, or an edge marker shows it is off the keyboard. |
| UR-05 | The student's range limits are marked on the piano wherever the piano is shown after range setup. |
| UR-06 | The current note name (and the current syllable in songs) is large enough to read at arm's length on the phone. |

### Lesson flow

| Id | Requirement |
|----|-------------|
| UR-07 | It is always clear which step is active (I do, We do, You do) and, in one short line, what the student should do right now. |
| UR-08 | "I do" can be repeated as many times as wanted with one tap. "We do" and "You do" can be retried with one tap. |
| UR-09 | Every run starts with a 4-click lead-in that is both heard and shown, so the student knows exactly when to start. |
| UR-10 | The student can see where they are in the exercise: which note is current, what has been sung, and what remains. |
| UR-11 | A run can be stopped at any moment with one visible control. |

### Feedback after singing

| Id | Requirement |
|----|-------------|
| UR-12 | Results show, for every note, whether it was hit or missed, and for misses the reason in plain words (no music theory needed). |
| UR-13 | Results show the score, the pass mark, and whether the lesson was passed, without scrolling. |
| UR-14 | Results give one concrete tip for what to change next time. |

### Range setup

| Id | Requirement |
|----|-------------|
| UR-15 | During range setup the note being held is shown live on the piano and by name. |
| UR-16 | The recording window is clearly announced: a countdown before it, and a visible indicator of how long remains while it is recording. |
| UR-17 | The recorded lowest and highest notes are shown and played back, and can be redone or adjusted before saving. |

### Tracker

| Id | Requirement |
|----|-------------|
| UR-18 | The home screen shows every lesson's status at a glance: not started, attempted with best score, or passed. |
| UR-19 | A lesson that does not fit the student's range is visibly unavailable and says why. |
| UR-20 | The next recommended lesson is one tap away from the home screen. |

### General

| Id | Requirement |
|----|-------------|
| UR-21 | Every screen works at laptop width (1280 px) and iPhone portrait (393 px) with no horizontal scrolling and nothing clipped or overlapping. |
| UR-22 | During a run, everything needed (piano, target, sung note, progress, stop control) is visible without scrolling the page. |
| UR-23 | Tap targets are at least 44 px in both dimensions on the phone. |
| UR-24 | The same meaning uses the same colour and wording on every screen. Meaning is never carried by colour alone; there is also a label, icon or position. |
| UR-25 | Problems are explained in plain words with the next action: microphone denied, no sound heard, no range set, lesson does not fit. |
| UR-26 | Every screen has an obvious way back to the home screen. Leaving a lesson stops sound and the microphone. |
| UR-27 | Text and controls are legible in both light and dark mode. |
